name: Tony Fadell
milestone_by_age_26: No material public breakout by age 26 found. University of Michigan CE B.S. 1991 (~22); systems architect at General Magic 1992–1995 (~23–26); hired at Philips in 1995 (~26) to co-found Mobile Computing Group as CTO—products (Velo/Nino) shipped ~1997 (~28). Fuse startup 1999 (~30); iPod contractor/hire 2001 (~32); Nest 2010 (~41).
early_history_summary: Born in Michigan to a Lebanese father and Polish mother; Grosse Pointe South High School and University of Michigan computer engineering (1991). Early career in handhelds at General Magic then Philips before the iPod and Nest eras that made him famous.
family_context_summary: Lebanese father and Polish mother; raised in Michigan. Family financial detail not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as consumer-electronics domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Defining public milestones (iPod 2001; Nest 2010–14) are well after age 26. Pre-26 record is strong engineering employment at General Magic and a Philips internal mobile group CTO role, not a dated independent product/company breakout with multi-source public impact by ≤26.

name: Jonathan Ive
milestone_by_age_26: No material public product breakout by age 26 found. Newcastle Polytechnic industrial design first-class BA 1989 (~22); RSA Student Design Awards 1988–89; Tangerine design agency work; joined Apple industrial design September 1992 (~25). MessagePad 110 work shipped 1994 (~27); iMac breakout 1998 (~31); SVP design late 1990s; CDO later.
early_history_summary: Born in Chingford, London; silversmith father Michael Ive lectured at Middlesex Polytechnic; family moved to Stafford around age 12. Dyslexia diagnosis in school; industrial design at Newcastle Polytechnic; London design agencies before Apple.
family_context_summary: Father Michael Ive was a silversmith and design lecturer; grandfather an engineer. Middle-class creative household in England.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father’s silversmithing/design teaching is domain-adjacent to industrial design.
evidence_summary: By age 26 Ive had elite design training and an Apple ID Group job, but the independently famous hardware milestones (iMac, iPod, iPhone era) arrived after 26. Student awards and early employment do not meet the material public breakout bar.

name: Craig Federighi
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. UC Berkeley EECS B.S. 1991 and CS M.S. 1993 (~22–24); engineer at NeXT (Enterprise Objects Framework) then Apple via NeXT acquisition 1996 (~27); left for Ariba 1999 (~30), returned Apple 2009 (~40); SVP software engineering 2012 (~43).
early_history_summary: Born in San Leandro, California; Berkeley EECS then CS graduate degrees. Built enterprise software at NeXT before the long Apple executive career that made him a public figure.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond San Leandro origin and Italian descent notes.
evidence_summary: Public notability as Apple’s software SVP is decades after age 26. Pre-26 path is strong education and early NeXT engineering without a dated, independently famous product/company milestone at ≤26.

name: Eddy Cue
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. Duke CS and economics degrees; joined Apple in 1989 (~24–25) in software engineering/customer support management. Major dated achievements—Apple online store (~1997, ~32–33), iTunes Store 2003 (~38), App Store 2008 (~43)—all after 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Miami to a Cuban mother and Spanish father; Duke University computer science and economics; long Apple career rising from early engineering/support management into services leadership.
family_context_summary: Son of a Cuban mother and Spanish father; met wife Paula at Duke. Early family financial detail not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as tech domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Joining Apple at ~25 is employment, not a material public product/company milestone. Documented breakout services work (online store, iTunes, App Store) is all post-26.

name: Phil Libin
milestone_by_age_26: In 1997, co-founded Boston software company Engine Five (Engine 5) as CEO with college friends, building online-store software for clients such as Nokia; the company was sold to Vignette in 2000 for about $26 million.
early_history_summary: Born in Leningrad (1972); emigrated to the U.S. in 1979 at age eight with classical-musician parents, settling in the Bronx. Bronx High School of Science (1989); studied CS at Boston University but left just before graduating to focus on freelancing and founding Engine 5 in 1997 at about age 25.
family_context_summary: Soviet immigrant family; parents classical musicians who left Leningrad in 1979 and lived with little money in a rough Bronx neighborhood after previously more comfortable Soviet life.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were classical musicians, not software/tech entrepreneurs.
primary_early_advantage_tags: college cofounders, immigrant constraint, early programming freelancing, Bronx Science, Engine 5 exit
evidence_summary: BBC documents Engine Five founded 1997 with Libin as CEO and sold three years later for $26M—clear dated founder milestone at age ~25. Immigrant constraint and teen freelancing programming support self-created technical reps rather than family capital. Later CoreStreet and Evernote amplify trajectory but the ≤26 gate is Engine 5.
starting_point: Born in Leningrad to classical-musician parents; emigrated to the Bronx in 1979 and grew up with limited money in a tough neighborhood while becoming a teenage computer nerd/freelancer.
current_position: Founder/operator of video presentation startup mmhmm and startup studio All Turtles; former Evernote CEO; proponent of remote work, based in Bentonville, Arkansas area.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Engine Five in Boston as CEO with college friends, building e-commerce software.
Sold Engine Five to Vignette for about $26 million near the peak of the dot-com era.
Co-founded CoreStreet (identity/credential security software), later sold for about $24 million.
Became CEO of Evernote after joining/merging with the note-taking product team.
Stepped down as Evernote CEO and joined General Catalyst as a general partner.
Built mmhmm and All Turtles after leaving Bay Area for Arkansas and championing remote work.

name: Eric Ries
milestone_by_age_26: In April 2004, co-founded IMVU Inc. with Will Harvey (and others) as co-founder and CTO, building a 3D avatar social network that later raised venture funding and became a multi-year growth company.
early_history_summary: Born 1978; published Black Art of Java Game Programming while in high school; Yale CS undergrad where he co-founded Catalyst Recruiting (dot-com, failed). After graduation worked at There, Inc., then co-founded IMVU in 2004 at age 25 as CTO.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yale CS, There.com to IMVU, Steve Blank mentorship, Silicon Valley 2000s, high school Java book
evidence_summary: Multi-source record shows IMVU co-founding/CTO role starting April 2004 when Ries was 25. Prior reps include a high-school Java book, a failed Yale-era startup, and There, Inc. engineering. Later lean-startup fame (2008–2011) builds on IMVU methods; mentor Steve Blank and SV ecosystem are documented accelerants.
starting_point: Not fully documented family origin; elite education path via Yale computer science after early programming publication in high school.
current_position: Author of The Lean Startup; founder/executive chair of Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE); entrepreneurship advisor and speaker.

trajectory.event: Moved to Silicon Valley after Yale as a software engineer at There, Inc.
Co-founded IMVU as co-founder and CTO with Will Harvey.
IMVU raised early venture capital (including Seraph Group) while practicing rapid deployment cycles.
Stepped down as IMVU CTO; coined 'lean startup' on his blog and began evangelizing the method.
Published The Lean Startup, which debuted at #2 on the New York Times bestseller list.
SEC approved Long-Term Stock Exchange, which Ries had organized as a new U.S. exchange concept.

name: Steve Blank
milestone_by_age_26: No material founder/operator breakout by age 26 found. Air Force service in Vietnam era (electronics on aircraft); early ESL/TRW training role after military. Serial startup career 1978–2002 and customer-development methodology/fame came much later (E.piphany 1996 ~43; Four Steps book mid-2000s; Lean LaunchPad ~2011).
early_history_summary: Born to Jewish immigrant parents in Chelsea, New York City; brief University of Michigan attendance; four years USAF electronic warfare/intelligence systems during Vietnam War period; entered Silicon Valley via ESL/TRW training work.
family_context_summary: Jewish immigrant parents in Chelsea, NYC; limited additional family financial detail in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/startup domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Blank’s defining contributions (customer development, lean entrepreneurship education, E.piphany) are mid-career and later. By age 26 the record is military technical service and early entry-level Silicon Valley training work—not a dated material founder milestone.

name: Naval Ravikant
milestone_by_age_26: In April 1999 (age 24), co-founded consumer product-review startup Epinions with Nirav Tolia and others; the company raised roughly $8M seed then ~$45M total VC from Benchmark and August Capital and became a high-profile late-1990s internet startup.
early_history_summary: Born in New Delhi (1974); moved to New York at age 9 with mother and brother Kamal; Stuyvesant High School 1991; Dartmouth CS and economics 1995; brief BCG then Silicon Valley. Co-founded Epinions at 24 before later building Venture Hacks/AngelList.
family_context_summary: Immigrated from New Delhi to New York City at age 9 with mother and brother; single-parent immigrant household details beyond that limited in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/venture domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stuyvesant, Dartmouth, dot-com wave, Epinions cofounders, Benchmark/August seed
evidence_summary: Epinions co-founding in 1999 at age 24 is multi-sourced (Wikipedia, NYT coverage of founders, company histories) and material: large VC raise and public internet notability. Immigrant trajectory plus elite schools and a complementary founder team explain early access more than family capital. Later AngelList (2010) is post-26 fame amplifier.
starting_point: Born in New Delhi; moved to New York City at age 9 with mother and brother; attended Stuyvesant and Dartmouth.
current_position: Co-founder/chairman of AngelList; angel investor, podcaster (nav.al), and author-related figure via The Almanack of Naval Ravikant; co-founded Airchat (2023).

trajectory.event: Graduated Dartmouth with computer science and economics degrees; brief BCG stint followed by Silicon Valley move.
Co-founded Epinions, raising multi-million seed from Benchmark and August Capital.
Epinions merged path into Shopping.com (IPO 2004); later founder lawsuit over merger economics settled in 2005.
Launched Hit Forge early-stage fund and Venture Hacks blog advising founders on term sheets.
Co-founded AngelList as a platform connecting startups and angel investors.
AngelList Venture raised capital at a roughly $4 billion valuation.

name: Keith Rabois
milestone_by_age_26: No material tech founder/operator milestone by age 26 found. Stanford BA 1991 (~22); Harvard JD 1994 (~25); federal appellate clerkship then nearly four years at Sullivan & Cromwell. PayPal EVP role began November 2000 (~31); later LinkedIn, Square COO, Opendoor cofounder, Khosla/Founders Fund.
early_history_summary: Raised in Edison, New Jersey; Stanford political science and Harvard Law; early career as lawyer and Quayle campaign adviser before switching into PayPal and Silicon Valley operating roles in his early 30s.
family_context_summary: Raised in Edison, New Jersey; family financial/occupation detail not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: By age 26 Rabois was a newly minted Harvard Law graduate entering big-law/clerkship tracks. Material tech operating milestones begin with PayPal in 2000 at ~31.

name: Roelof Botha
milestone_by_age_26: No material public operator/founder milestone by age 26 found. UCT actuarial science/econ/stats BSc 1996 (~22–23) with exceptional GPA; McKinsey Johannesburg 1996–98; Stanford GSB MBA (valedictorian). Joined PayPal corporate development in 2000 (~26–27); named CFO September 2001 (~27–28); Sequoia partner 2003 (~29–30).
early_history_summary: Born Pretoria 1973; raised in Cape Town’s Hout Bay; grandson of South African foreign minister Pik Botha. Top UCT undergraduate, McKinsey analyst, then Stanford MBA before PayPal finance leadership and Sequoia career.
family_context_summary: South African political family; grandfather Pik Botha was foreign minister. Father described as an economist in some profiles.
parent_family_domain_summary: Political/economic elite family; not a tech-product domain apprenticeship documented.
evidence_summary: Elite academics and consulting by 26, but PayPal CFO (2001) and Sequoia partnership (2003) are after 26. Joining PayPal as an employee around the age-26 boundary is not treated as a material independent founder/breakout milestone.

name: David Sacks
category: Entrepreneur and investor (PayPal, Yammer, Craft Ventures)
milestone_by_age_26: No material founder/company breakout by age 26 found. Stanford BA 1994 (~22); co-authored The Diversity Myth with Peter Thiel 1995 (~23) (political/academic, not operator milestone); University of Chicago JD 1998 (~26); McKinsey then joined Confinity/PayPal in 1999 (~26–27) as early product leader/later COO—employee not cofounder. Yammer founding 2008 (~36).
early_history_summary: Born Cape Town to a Jewish family; emigrated to Tennessee at age five; father an endocrinologist. Memphis University School; Stanford economics; Chicago Law; entered PayPal via Thiel network after McKinsey.
family_context_summary: Jewish family from Cape Town; father an endocrinologist; grandfather ran a candy factory that inspired entrepreneurship stories.
parent_family_domain_summary: Medical professional father; grandfather’s candy business is entrepreneurial but not tech domain.
evidence_summary: Law school completion at ~26 and joining PayPal as an early employee around 26–27 do not equal a ≤26 founder breakout. Defining company founding (Yammer) and later Craft Ventures/political roles are well after 26.

name: Bret Taylor
category: Software engineer and product executive (Google Maps, FriendFeed, Salesforce, Sierra)
milestone_by_age_26: As a Google associate product manager (joined 2003), led the team that built Google Local / co-created Google Maps; Google Maps launched publicly in early 2005 when Taylor was about 24–25, becoming a landmark consumer web product.
early_history_summary: Born in Oakland (1980), raised in the East Bay; Acalanes High School 1998; Stanford CS B.S. 2002 and M.S. 2003 (parents and older sister also Stanford). Hired by Marissa Mayer into Google’s APM program; led location/maps work that became Google Maps before leaving in 2007 to found FriendFeed.
family_context_summary: East Bay California upbringing; multi-generation Stanford family (parents and older sister also attended).
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as professional software-engineering domain transfer beyond elite academic family culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, Google APM, Marissa Mayer hire, pre-IPO Google, Maps launch 2005
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, First Round/Fast Company lessons, and contemporary product histories credit Taylor with leading Google Local/Maps work culminating in the 2005 Maps launch at age ~25—material, multi-sourced, and within ≤26. Advantage stack is elite institutions + Bay Area/Google platform rather than inherited startup capital. Later FriendFeed, Facebook CTO, Quip, Salesforce co-CEO, Sierra, and OpenAI chair continue the arc.
starting_point: Born in Oakland and raised in California’s East Bay; multi-generation Stanford family; Stanford CS bachelor’s and master’s by 2003.
current_position: Co-founder of AI company Sierra; chairman of OpenAI’s board; Shopify board member; former Salesforce co-CEO and former Facebook CTO.

trajectory.event: Joined Google’s associate product manager program under Marissa Mayer after Stanford CS degrees.
Google Maps publicly launched from the Google Local/maps work his team led.
Left Google for Benchmark EIR and co-founded FriendFeed as CEO.
FriendFeed acquired by Facebook (~$50M); later became Facebook CTO (2010).
Left Facebook to found collaborative productivity company Quip.
Named Salesforce co-CEO/vice chair after leading product and Slack acquisition work.
Co-founded AI startup Sierra and became OpenAI board chair after the Altman ouster/reinstatement.
